prompt: Create a high-fidelity landscape desktop web dashboard screen comp, 1440 by 1000 pixels. Structure first: a quiet fixed Ovok navigation rail on the left; a broad patient review workspace on the right. At top show the single CHF clinic, a compact patient switcher, and patient identity with a visible Demo data label. The central focal region is the selected patient's latest check-in, containing three peer measurement panels side by side: a short ECG rhythm trace with recording time and source Viatom BP2; a weight reading with a small seven-day trend and source LeScale; and a short questionnaire summary with a time stamp. Below, show a simple chronological recent-activity list with two entries and understated links to patient history and the clinic review queue. The screen's visitor job must read at a glance as reviewing one patient's most recent CHF RPM readings, with all three measurements visible together and no suggested diagnosis or clinical action. Include realistic fictional patient name and age, synthetic demo values, readable dates and units, and exact concise labels where possible: Ovok, Home, Patients, Signals setup, Help, CHF clinic, Patient overview, Latest check-in, ECG, Weight, Questionnaire, Viatom BP2, LeScale, View history. Use the reference Ovok mobile app only for the identity: purple wordmark character, near-white lavender canvas, deep purple #4B356D, accent purple #694D98, pale lilac #F0EBF7, dark plum-black #24202D, rounded white surfaces, gentle corners, clean system sans type. Adapt this identity to a refined clinician web workspace with precise alignment, strong reading order, comfortable information density, restrained dividers, and accessible contrast. Do not copy phone chrome, mobile layout, tab bar, home hero copy, or screen content. No photographs, gradients, glass effects, heavy shadows, extra clinics or organizations, invented alert thresholds, diagnostic conclusions, or treatment recommendations. This is a usable product interface comp, not a poster. All people and values are synthetic demo data.
